evals.prompt: I need to hook our Entra tenant (contoso.onmicrosoft.com) up to SailPoint ISC — tenant is contoso-sb.api.identitynow-demo.com. Read-only for now, we just want users, groups and roles aggregated for certifications. I'm Global Admin but I don't want anything created yet: give me exactly what you'd run on both sides and show me the dry-run plan. I don't have az logged in on this machine right now.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Microsoft Entra SaaS connector (not the VA one); produces a plan-only/dry-run of the Entra app registration with read-only Graph application permissions (User.Read.All, Group.Read.All, Organization.Read.All, RoleManagement.Read.Directory), consent, secret to a file; the ISC sequence discover/create/configure/peek/aggregate; nothing applied; no secret values requested in chat.
assertions: Names the cloud Microsoft Entra (SaaS) connector, not the VA-based Azure Active Directory connector
Entra plan includes the read-only Graph application permissions User.Read.All, Group.Read.All, Organization.Read.All and RoleManagement.Read.Directory
Entra plan contains no write permissions (no User.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All)
Includes an admin consent / grant step for the application permissions
Client secret is handled without asking the user to paste it into chat (written to a file / not echoed)
ISC side covers create + configure (domainName contoso.onmicrosoft.com, clientID, clientSecret, grantType) with a concrete dry-run/plan shown for the ISC calls too
Proof-of-work steps are peek, then test connection, then aggregation
No ISC call in the plan uses a /beta/ endpoint
Nothing is created: no --apply / no write commands were executed
ISC calls shown use the v2026 API

evals.prompt: We're onboarding Entra ID into IdentityNow with full lifecycle: joiner/mover/leaver provisioning, Exchange Online mailboxes and distribution lists, plus PIM eligible roles so certifiers see them. Our Entra admin will apply things herself, so list every single template/file I need to apply on the Entra side and on the SailPoint side, what each one contains, and which directory roles the app ends up with. Save the list to a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: Markdown inventory covering Entra app manifest, permission sets for provisioning/exchange/pim (Exchange.ManageAsApp on Office 365 Exchange Online), consent bodies, directory roles (User Administrator, Exchange Administrator; Privileged Authentication Administrator only opt-in), certificate auth for Exchange, ISC source create body, configure patch (domainName, clientID, clientSecret, grantType), feature toggles, schedule.
assertions: A markdown file listing the templates was saved in outputs
Lists an Entra app registration / manifest template
Lists provisioning Graph application permissions incl. User.ReadWrite.All and Group.ReadWrite.All, without Directory.ReadWrite.All
Lists Exchange.ManageAsApp on Office 365 Exchange Online and certificate-based auth for Exchange
Lists read-only PIM permissions (e.g. PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Read.AzureADGroup / RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory), not ReadWrite PIM permissions
States the app ends up with User Administrator and Exchange Administrator directory roles, and no Global Administrator
SailPoint side lists a source-creation body and a connection-settings body (domainName, clientID, clientSecret, grantType)
SailPoint side includes a CREATE provisioning policy template for joiners
SailPoint side covers leaver/joiner account actions (lifecycle state) or correlation
SailPoint side includes aggregation (schedule or aggregation step), and no listed SailPoint endpoint is /beta/
Connector setting names are either verified or explicitly flagged as unverified (no invented keys presented as fact)

evals.prompt: our sailpoint entra source 'Entra ID - Fabrikam' keeps failing test connection with AADSTS7000215 and when I fixed something last week aggregation then gave 403 Authorization_RequestDenied 'Insufficient privileges to complete the operation' on create account. what's going on and how do I fix it with az cli? app id is 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8a-9c0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f
evals.expected_output: Explains AADSTS7000215 = secret ID used instead of Value / wrong or expired secret, shows creating a new secret with az ad app credential reset --append into a file and reconfiguring; explains 403 = missing/unconsented Graph application permission (User.ReadWrite.All etc.), that Global Admin role doesn't substitute, how to check granted appRoleAssignments and grant with az; mentions User Administrator for passwords.
assertions: Explains AADSTS7000215 as the secret ID used instead of its Value, or a wrong secret, and distinguishes an expired secret (AADSTS7000222)
Gives an az ad app credential reset command using the provided app id with --append
The new secret value is written to a protected file or vault, not printed to the terminal
Explains the 403 as a missing or unconsented Microsoft Graph application permission
Names User.ReadWrite.All as the permission needed to create accounts
Shows how to check which application permissions are actually granted (appRoleAssignments)
Shows how to grant admin consent with az (admin-consent or appRoleAssignments POST)
Mentions that a Global Administrator role does not replace Graph permissions, or that User Administrator is needed for password set
After the fix, re-verifies with peek, test connection and aggregation (any ISC calls non-beta)
ISC calls shown use the v2026 API

evals.prompt: The Entra source 'Entra ID - Contoso' is already created and configured in our ISC tenant (acme.api.identitynow.com). Prove it actually works and pull everything in: accounts, entitlements, and the Azure AI Foundry agents dataset. Our security team doesn't allow beta APIs in production, so GA endpoints only, and we standardise on the v2026 API. I don't have the PAT on this machine, so show me exactly which calls you'd make and in what order.
evals.expected_output: Plan of peek -> test -> aggregation using v2026 endpoints only: peek-resource-objects, test-configuration, load-entitlements, load-accounts (multipart disableOptimization), aggregate-agents with datasetIds [azure:foundry] + experimental header, task-status polling; notes that the Foundry dataset needs enableAIFoundryAgent + Azure RBAC; no /beta/.
assertions: Order is peek, then test connection, then aggregation
No /beta/ endpoint anywhere in the plan
Peek and test use /v2026/sources/{id}/connector/peek-resource-objects and .../connector/test-configuration (v2026)
Aggregation covers entitlements, accounts and the dataset
Account aggregation uses POST /v2026/sources/{id}/load-accounts as multipart/form-data (disableOptimization)
Dataset aggregation uses POST /v2026/sources/{id}/aggregate-agents with datasetIds including azure:foundry
Notes that aggregate-agents (and the dataset list) need the X-SailPoint-Experimental header
Polls aggregation tasks with a GA task-status endpoint (/v2026/task-status/{id})
Notes the Foundry dataset must be enabled on the source (enableAIFoundryAgent / aggregationEnabled) and needs Azure-side access
Every ISC call is on /v2026/ (no v3/v2025 mixing)
